text:
rachel_sales: Heads-up — Acme POC failing when the client is behind their corporate proxy. TS SDK calls intermittently error with socket hangups, customer says curl -> proxy works though. Can someone help triage?

devon_se: what SDK version and node version? also paste the raw error/logs if you have them.

rachel_sales: sdk@1.8.2, node 18. got this from the app logs:
```
Error: socket hang up
    at TLSSocket.onHangUp (_http_client.js:XXXX:XX)
    at TLSSocket.emit (events.js:XXX:XX)
    at endReadableNT (internal/streams/readable.js:XXX:XX)
Caused-by: ECONNRESET
```
Will paste more if helpful.

alex_dev: common pattern when a corporate proxy is dropping idle connections. Are you using an HTTP proxy agent with keepAlive? default agent will open new sockets frequently -> proxy idle closes them.

katie_devex: quick checklist: HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY set? no_proxy for internal addresses? PAC or NTLM in use?

rachel_sales: yes HTTPS_PROXY is set in env. It's a chained proxy with auth. Not NTLM. No PAC.

sam_ops: two things to try: (1) enable keepAlive on the proxy agent (2) increase socket timeout and retry backoff. Also check proxy idle timeout (some corp proxies default 60s).

alex_dev: snippet to use with node TS SDK client (we've shared variations to other customers):
```
import HttpsProxyAgent from 'https-proxy-agent';
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY);
agent.keepAlive = true;
agent.keepAliveMsecs = 10000;
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, agent, timeoutMs: 120000 });
```
That keeps connections warm through the proxy.

devon_se: also set retries/backoff in the SDK config. Example: { maxRetries: 3, retryDelayMs: 500, retryBackoff: 2 }. If proxy returns 502/504 we should exponential backoff instead of immediate reconnect storms.

rachel_sales: tried agent + keepAlive, still seeing occasional 504s: `504 upstream connect timeout` from proxy. They say proxy logs show connection idle.

sam_ops: could be the proxy's idle TCP timeout shorter than your app-level keep-alive. Two options: bump proxy idle on their infra (ask their infra team) or reduce frequency of new connections (use connection pooling / persistent sockets).

katie_devex: another workaround: switch the SDK to fewer parallel connections (lower concurrency) or enable SDK-side prefix caching/batching so we send fewer requests. That reduces new connection churn.

alex_dev: also try enabling streaming: false (or disable chunked requests) — some proxies treat chunked streaming as long-running and close. If you can accept non-streamed responses in POC, that often stabilizes it.

rachel_sales: security asked if Redwood supports mTLS through the proxy. They want outbound client certs to upstream. Is that supported?

devon_se: outbound mTLS from the customer proxy -> Redwood is compatible, but the client (our SDK) would need to present certs to the proxy. Node https-proxy-agent supports `pfx`/`cert`/`key` options. For full mTLS to Redwood you'd need a direct TLS with mTLS; if proxy terminates TLS you'd present certs to proxy only. For company-mandated mTLS e2e you may need Dedicated/private deployment or a tunnel.

rachel_sales: ok I'll confirm with their security team. Also they mentioned a corporate appliance that enforces 30s idle — that seems tight.

support_bot: Created support ticket POCTRIAGE-421 for AcmeCorp POC and linked this thread.

sam_ops: next steps: 1) ask Acme infra to increase proxy idle timeout to 120s OR enable TCP keepalive there, 2) try SDK agent keepAlive + timeoutMs 120000 and maxRetries 3, 3) test disabling streaming/chunking, 4) if they require mTLS end-to-end escalate to dedicated/private options.

rachel_sales: will run tests with agent + increased timeouts and report results. thanks all. :thumbsup:

alex_dev: happy to pair if you want — ping me when they run the test.

katie_devex: doc link for proxy troubleshooting: https://redwood.example/docs/sdk/proxy (internal)

rachel_sales: noted — closing loop after tests. Cheers!
